note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Card, other: The card restates the definition of the median ('the middle value in order'), which belongs to point 2 (Mean, median, mode and range). It should only mention the median here, not define it.

rejected.title: Choosing a measure of centre
card: An outlier is a value far from the rest of the data. It can be much higher or much lower than the other values.
Mean
uses every value in its total, so an outlier pulls the mean towards it. One very high value makes the mean higher.
Median
is the middle value in order. An outlier is just one value at the end, so the median barely moves.
Example: 3, 4, 4, 5, 39. The mean is 55 ÷ 5 = 11 and the median is 4. Most values are near 4, so the median describes the centre better here.
rejected.remember: An outlier drags the mean towards it, so with extreme values the median often describes the centre better.

a.q: Five students sent 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18 messages yesterday. The mean is 6 and the median is 3. Which describes the centre better, and why?
opts: The median, because the outlier 18 pulls the mean up
The mean, because it uses every value in the data
The median, because it is always the larger of the two
The mean, because the outlier 18 does not affect it
a.why: Four of the five values are 4 or less, so a mean of 6 is higher than almost all of them. The outlier 18 pulls the mean up, while the median stays at 3. Using every value is true of the mean, but here it is a weakness.
a.clue: Compare each centre with where most of the values sit.

b.q: Weekly pocket money for five students is $10, $12, $13, $15 and $5. The $5 value is replaced by $60. What happens to the mean and the median?
opts: The mean rises a lot and the median rises a little
The mean rises a little and the median rises a lot
The mean and the median both rise by the same amount
The mean stays the same and the median rises a lot
b.why: Before: the total is 55, so the mean is 55 ÷ 5 = $11, and in order 5, 10, 12, 13, 15 the median is $12. After: the total is 110, so the mean is $22, and in order 10, 12, 13, 15, 60 the median is $13. The mean rises by $11 but the median rises by only $1, so they do not rise by the same amount.
b.clue: Put the values in order and find both centres before and after.

opts: The mean rises a lot and the median rises a little

problems.detail: With six values, the median is the average of the two middle values: (10+12)/2 = 11 before and (12+14)/2 = 13 after. The card only defines the median as 'the middle value in order' and uses an odd-count example. Students who follow the card alone may get stuck, and the why does not show the averaging step.
